movement_profile.arms_and_hands: female dancers carry and gesture with a decorated staff (kiyaya or chuncho); the yunca holds and manipulates a leather whip or rein (culebrilla)
movement_profile.formation_and_space: quadrilla group formation involving spatial interactions between capitana, six pallas, yunca, and gurikuq
movement_profile.partnering: group dramatic interaction between the male yunca character and the female pallas
movement_profile.posture: bent or twisted posture suggested by the alternate name wiqru palla, carried out with deliberate regal bearing

signature_moves.description: Female dancers hold decorated staves (kiyaya/chuncho) while performing choreography.
signature_moves.name: Kiyaya staff holding

signature_moves.description: The yunca character handles a whip/rein prop while navigating around the female dancers.
signature_moves.name: Culebrilla manipulation

movement_profile.tempo_feel: progresses across four phases ending in the festive chimaychi stage
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: avoid disrespecting traditional character attire and prop placement

music_profile.sound_description: A traditional Andean soundscape produced by a duo consisting of a single woodwind flute playing melodious themes over the steady beat of a small traditional drum (caja).

teaching.formation: cuadrilla line and figure formation consisting of one capitana, six pallas, a yunca, and a gurikuq
teaching.level_notes: requires understanding of character roles and execution of four distinct sequence stages
teaching.rhythm: rhythmic accompaniment provided by flauta and caja
